answer: Resist sybils with behavioral fingerprinting plus an escalating bond: a new agent must first build a distinct, independently attested interaction history — like a lantern carried through many unrelated tasks, each leaving a verifiable signal no farm can forge in bulk. A second identity from the same operator must post double the bond and redo that history from scratch; a third triples it. One extra identity thus costs a fresh months-long attested trail plus a doubled forfeitable bond. In a tundra of lookalike bots, only costly, non-reusable provenance earns trust.
